O1: Can a new potential customer understand what you sell within a few seconds?
O2: Does your primary offer promise a clear outcome or improvement?
O3: How clearly defined is the customer your offer is for?
O4: How often do qualified prospects question the value, price, or reason to choose your offer?
O5: How much evidence do you have that people actually want this offer?
O6: If qualified traffic doubled tomorrow, how confident are you in the current sales experience?
A1: How clearly can you identify the customers who get the most value from your offer?
A2: Do your best customers share a specific problem, trigger, or situation that causes them to look?
A3: How often are your leads or prospects actually a good fit?
A4: How well do you understand what your customer is ultimately trying to accomplish?
A5: If you needed to reach 1,000 ideal prospects, do you know who they are and where to reach them?
M1: Can a new visitor understand your main value within the first few seconds?
M2: Does your marketing focus more on customer outcomes or on what you provide?
M3: How closely does your marketing use the words your customers actually use?
M4: Can a potential customer quickly understand why they should choose you over another reasonable option?
M5: Does your message give people an emotional reason to care?
M6: How much credible evidence supports the important claims in your marketing?
C1: Is the next action you want a visitor to take immediately clear?
C2: How much work does a visitor have to do before understanding why the next step is worthwhile?
C3: Does the promise that gets someone there match what they see after the click?
C4: How much unnecessary friction exists between interest and conversion?
C5: How strong is the proof or reassurance near the point of action?
C6: Does the experience match the level of commitment you are asking for?
T1: Do you understand which traffic sources bring in new people versus bring people back?
T2: Do you know whether enough new demand is entering the system?
T3: When performance changes, how confidently can you identify the real cause?
T4: Do your acquisition channels have clearly defined roles?
T5: Are your tests set up with enough budget and volume to teach you something useful?
T6: Do you know what you can reasonably afford to spend to acquire a lead or customer?
ML1: Have you clearly defined the few business outcomes that matter most?
ML2: Do you distinguish outcome KPIs from diagnostic KPIs?
ML3: Do you maintain a consistent KPI report or dashboard over time?
ML4: Does your team agree on which numbers to trust and where they come from?
ML5: Can you connect marketing activity to downstream business outcomes?
ML6: When performance changes, do you investigate before making major decisions?
